sources.description: Global provenance: every source that contributed to this dataset.

id.description: Short id referenced by instruction.provenance entries, e.g. 'felix', 'xed', 'uops'.

version.description: Source revision, e.g. SDM revision number or XED git sha.

conventions.description: Normative rules this dataset follows. Consumers can rely on these — they are not descriptive.

opcode_normalization.description: The 0F / 0F38 / 0F3A escape bytes MUST be encoded in encodings.prefix_map, never as leading bytes of encodings.opcode. So 0F B6 is always {prefix_map:'0F', opcode:'B6'} — never {prefix_map:'legacy', opcode:'0F B6'}.

modes_completeness.description: instruction.modes MUST emit all four booleans (real, protected, long_64, compat_32). No implicit defaults.

boolean_absence.description: For optional booleans on encodings (modrm, rex_w, evex.broadcast, evex.sae, evex.rounding_control, operand.broadcast, operand.mask_allowed, operand.signed): absent MUST be treated as false. Emitters SHOULD omit false rather than write it explicitly, to keep files small; consumers MUST NOT distinguish absent from false.

flags_absence.description: In instruction.flags, an absent key means the flag is unchanged. There is deliberately no 'unchanged' enum value.

vendor_semantics.description: An instruction's top-level fields are its BASELINE. The baseline describes Intel's documentation for any form Intel documents, and the sole implementing vendor otherwise. Where another vendor differs, instruction.vendor_overrides.<vendor> restates only the differing keys, and each key present there REPLACES the baseline key wholesale for that vendor (never merged). No override for a vendor means that vendor matches the baseline. instruction.vendor_exclusive is set only where single-vendor implementation is known; its absence records no claim either way.

operand_size_forms.description: 16/32/64-bit variants of the same mnemonic MUST be separate instruction entries, distinguished by encoding.default_operand_size plus the operand_size_prefix / rex_w fields on their encodings. Do not collapse them into a single entry with a variable size.

id_uniqueness.description: instruction.id MUST be unique across the entire instructions[] array. JSON Schema cannot enforce this; validators MUST check it as a pipeline step.

groups.description: Reusable groupings referenced from instruction.groups by id.

id.description: Unique per (mnemonic, operand signature). MUST be globally unique across instructions[]; validators must check this — JSON Schema cannot express it. See conventions.id_uniqueness.

vendor_exclusive.description: Present only when this form is known to be implemented by one vendor alone (e.g. VMX and SGX are Intel-only; SVM and XOP are AMD-only). Absence is NOT a claim that both vendors implement it — it means no exclusivity has been recorded. See conventions.vendor_semantics.

vendor_overrides.description: Vendor-specific deviations from this instruction's baseline fields. See conventions.vendor_semantics.

provenance.description: Per-instruction citations. Each entry points at a source declared in top-level sources[] and optionally a specific page/URL/section.

url.description: Deep link, e.g. the felixcloutier.com page for this mnemonic.

prefix_map.description: Escape/opcode map. Required. Use 'legacy' for single-byte opcodes with no escape. See conventions.opcode_normalization.

opcode.description: Hex bytes of the primary opcode AFTER the map is stripped. For 0F B6, this is 'B6'. For 0F 38 F0, this is 'F0'.

opcode_suffix.description: Trailing byte AFTER the ModR/M (and any displacement) that selects the operation, rather than an immediate operand. Used by 3DNow!, whose forms all encode as 0F 0F /r <suffix>.

default_operand_size.description: Default operand size for this encoding in its listed modes, before any size prefixes apply. Required for legacy encodings (no VEX/EVEX). Forbidden for VEX/EVEX encodings, where operand width comes from vex.length / evex.length and the element type from the opcode. Combined with operand_size_prefix and rex_w to derive the effective size for legacy forms.

operand_size_prefix.description: How the 66h prefix interacts with this encoding. 'toggles' = flips between the mode's default and the alternate size (the usual 16<->32 dance). 'required'/'forbidden' cover forms where 66h is architecturally fixed. 'ignored' for encodings unaffected (most vector forms).

address_size_prefix.description: Same idea for the 67h address-size prefix.

allOf.description: default_operand_size is required for legacy encodings and forbidden for the vector-prefix encodings, where width comes from the prefix instead.
vex, evex and xop are mutually exclusive on a single encoding.

modes.description: All four booleans MUST be present per the modes_completeness convention.

flags.description: Absent key = unchanged. Present key = one of the flag_effect values.

vendor_override.description: How one vendor deviates from the instruction's baseline fields. A key present here REPLACES the corresponding baseline key wholesale for that vendor — values are never merged. 'note' is mandatory so every deviation states what differs and why.

flag_effect.description: There is intentionally no 'unchanged' value — omit the key instead. See conventions.flags_absence.

xop.description: XOP prefix fields (AMD XOP, TBM and LWP). The 8Fh-escaped analogue of VEX; maps 8/9/A are disjoint from the VEX maps.
